newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends lower after morning rally.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends lower after morning rally.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled lower after a morning rally, undermined by some late profit taking and hedge selling, industry sources said.
"Enough people were looking at the higher cash prices as a selling (hedge) opportunity," said one Houston-based futures trader.
Forecasts for next week also called for warmer weather in the West, with expectations heating loads and power demand in the Northwest would be reduced, the traders said.

May California Oregon Border (COB) finished down 25 cents at $11.80 after trade at $11.70-12.30, while June settled down 30 cents at the day's low of $11.90 after reaching as high as $12.30 per megawatt hour (MWh).
Remaining COB deferreds closed the day down between 10 and 36 cents following morning and early afternoon trade that was above Tuesday settlements.
May Palo Verde (PV) ended down 20 cents at $15.40 per MWh after trade at $15.35-15.75, while June settled down 13 cents at the day's low of $16.40 from trade as high as $16.85 per MWh.
Remaining PV deferreds closed down between five and 15 cents after a morning of higher values.
Over the short-term, power supplies in the Northwest were expected to be reduced as hydroelectric projects spilled water for fish migrations.
Spillage on the Snake River, which feeds into the Columbia River basin, was scheduled to begin on Thursday, while the fish flush on the Columbia River was set to start April 20.
Cash prices were said to be continuing strong in the West, with the region under the influence of below-normal temperatures.

Temperatures in the Pacific Northwest were expected to be 12 to 24 degrees Fahrenheit below normal east of the Continental Divide through Sunday. Temperatures were expected to be near-normal along the coast during the same period.
Cooler temperatures were also seen impacting Northwest hydroelectric generation by delaying the rate of snowmelt and reducing the amount of water runoff over the short term.
Above-normal precipitation and below-normal temperatures were forecast for the Southwest over the next five days.
Longer-term forecasts called for above-normal temperatures in the Southwest from April 15-19, while the Northwest was expected to be above normal along the coast and near-normal inland.
Several generation facilities in the West remained shut for maintenance, together making up about 5,000 megawatts of power capacity that was out of service.
Also, the 1,087 MW Diablo Canyon 2 nuclear unit was operating at 50 percent power after being shut for unplanned repairs 12 days ago.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 571 COB and 369 PV contracts were traded Wednesday.
